title: Pragmatic OOD in Go
summary: Interfaces, composition and SOLID the Go way: small interfaces at the consumer, constructors, errors as values, package boundaries, testability.

labs.title: Refactor a god-object order manager: consumer-side interfaces, validating constructor, injected fakes and clock, parity with legacy
Refactor a string-error, global-state event dispatcher: typed errors, wrapping, injected time, concurrency-safe, extensible by tests

outcomes.text: Diagnose a god object by its reasons to change and ambient state, and refactor it behind a characterisation (parity) test one seam at a time.
Explain Go's object model without inheritance: method sets, embedding as composition (promotion, no virtual dispatch), and when to embed versus use a named field.
Define small interfaces at the consumer, accept interfaces and return structs, and say when not to define an interface.
Design constructors that enforce invariants: required dependencies, functional options versus a config struct, defensive copies, immutability, and a deliberate zero-value story.
Choose pointer or value receivers, avoid copying locks, and explain and avoid the typed-nil-in-interface trap.
Use errors as values: sentinel, typed and behaviour errors, %w wrapping with errors.Is/As/Join, handle-once logging, and mapping domain errors to transport codes at the edge only.
Structure packages by domain with the dependency pointing at the core, break import cycles, and avoid util/common packages.
Translate each SOLID principle into idiomatic Go and write a contract test for a plug-in interface.
Design for tests: seams for time, IDs, network and filesystem, fakes versus mocks, table-driven tests, golden files and httptest.
Run a 45-minute LLD round: model entities and responsibilities, pick the one or two interfaces that matter, and absorb a mid-way requirement change by adding code behind an existing seam.
Choose between generics and interfaces for containers and plug-in points.
Recognise and unwind premature abstraction using a checklist (second implementation, test seam, behaviour versus data).
